value.body: A medical records executive works in a hospital's medical records department (MRD), keeping patient files complete, organised and confidential. Hospitals and diagnostic chains hire for this work. A typical day involves checking discharge files, indexing records in the hospital information system, and retrieving files for doctors, audits and insurance claims.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA (Hospital Management), B.Sc or a medical records course

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Hospital information system (HIS), ICD codes, spreadsheets

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a hospital MRD as an executive or assistant. A short course in medical records or ICD coding, and familiarity with NABH documentation requirements, make entry easier.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Data entry in HIS and spreadsheets

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: MRD in-charge, medical coder, quality or health-information roles.
As hospitals move to electronic records, the work shifts toward digital systems.
Hospital-based work, with shift duties in larger hospitals.

value.title: Health records linked to ABHA
value.note: Dates are not evenly spaced. Counts are records linked digitally, not patients; shows the shift to digital records that MRD staff handle.
value.source: PIB documents on Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (Feb 2024, Nov 2024, Jul 2026)
